title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra Leads Open Models on Accuracy and Efficiency in Agentic RTL Coding | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Ultra model paired with the ACE-RTL agentic coding loop tops open models GLM 5.2 and Kimi K2.6 on the CVDP hardware-design benchmark (97.1% average pass rate) while using up to 71% fewer tokens per iteration, and NVIDIA has lined up Cadence, Siemens, and Synopsys to embed it in their EDA agent tooling.

insights.claim: ACE-RTL running with Nemotron 3 Ultra achieves a 97.1% average pass rate across nine CVDP agentic RTL task categories, beating the same agent loop run with Kimi K2.6 (95.2%) and GLM 5.2 (92.1%).
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: When agent scaffolding is held constant, the base model choice is worth roughly 5 points of pass rate on realistic hardware-design tasks — a concrete axis for comparing open coding models beyond generic leaderboards.
insights.quote: ACE-RTL with Nemotron 3 Ultra delivers the strongest overall performance, with a 97.1% average pass rate, compared with 95.2% for Kimi K2.6 and 92.1% for GLM 5.2.

insights.claim: Wrapping GLM 5.2 in the ACE-RTL iterative generate-test-reflect loop lifts its pass rate on the CVDP debugging/bug-fixing category from 44.0% as a standalone model to 94.3%, showing agentic tooling can matter more than the underlying model for this task type.
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: Vendors comparing 'raw' open models without an agent harness are understating real deployable capability; investors evaluating coding-LLM competitiveness should weight tooling/agent design as heavily as base-model quality.
insights.quote: GLM 5.2 improves from 44.0% as a standalone model to 94.3% with ACE-RTL

insights.claim: Nemotron 3 Ultra's standalone pass rate on CVDP debugging tasks rises from 65.7% to 100.0% once placed inside the ACE-RTL agent loop, the only one of the three tested models to reach a perfect score on that category.
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: A 100% score on a debugging benchmark category is a strong marketing data point NVIDIA can cite when selling Nemotron into EDA-agent partnerships.

insights.claim: In the ACE-RTL loop, Nemotron 3 Ultra uses 6,629 tokens per iteration on average versus 9,156 for GLM 5.2 and 22,579 for Kimi K2.6 — about 28% fewer tokens than GLM 5.2 and 71% fewer than Kimi K2.6 — while still posting the highest pass rate of the three.
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: Token cost compounds across many agent iterations; a model that is simultaneously more accurate and cheaper per step directly lowers the inference bill for enterprise agentic-coding deployments, a competitive lever against Chinese open-weight rivals GLM and Kimi/Moonshot.
insights.quote: 6,629 tokens per iteration on average, compared with 9,156 for GLM 5.2 and 22,579 for Kimi K2.6
insights.locator: Importantly, Nemotron 3 Ultra achieves this accuracy

insights.claim: Combining higher pass rate with lower per-iteration token usage means more unique RTL problems can be attempted within a fixed compute budget and engineers get results faster, framed explicitly as the practical payoff of accuracy-plus-efficiency in agentic settings.
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: For buyers sizing agentic-coding infra spend, token efficiency should be evaluated jointly with accuracy, not as a separate cost line — cheaper-but-less-accurate or accurate-but-expensive models both lose on this framing.
insights.quote: more RTL tasks can be attempted within the same compute budget, and engineers can get results faster
insights.locator: This combination of higher accuracy and lower token cost

insights.claim: Nemotron 3 Ultra is a 550B total-parameter, 55B active-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with a hybrid Mamba-Attention architecture, pretrained on 20 trillion text tokens and extended to a 1M-token context length.
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: A 55B active/550B total sparse MoE design lets NVIDIA claim frontier-class long-context reasoning at a fraction of the active-parameter inference cost of dense models of similar total size.
insights.quote: a 550B total-parameter, 55B active-parameter Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Attention model
insights.locator: Nemotron 3 Ultra is built for long-running agentic reasoning

insights.claim: NVIDIA attributes Nemotron 3 Ultra's efficiency to its hybrid Mamba-Attention design cutting attention cost and KV-cache footprint while its MoE structure improves accuracy per active parameter, together claimed to deliver up to 5x higher throughput and 30% lower cost than other open models.
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: Architecture (hybrid state-space + MoE) is becoming a distinct competitive axis for long-context agentic inference cost, separate from raw benchmark accuracy — worth tracking against pure-Transformer competitors as a cost-of-inference differentiator.
insights.quote: delivering up to 5X higher throughput and 30% lower costs compared to other open models
insights.locator: The hybrid Mamba-Attention architecture improves the throughput efficiency

insights.claim: ACE-RTL is structured as three cooperating components — a generator that produces/updates RTL, a reflector that diagnoses simulation failures and gives fix guidance, and a coordinator that maintains an evolving debugging context across iterations so the agent doesn't repeat past mistakes.
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: The generator/reflector/coordinator split with persistent evolving context is a reusable agentic-coding template applicable beyond RTL to any domain with tool-based verification feedback (compilers, test suites), relevant to how agentic-coding startups architect their own loops.

insights.claim: Nemotron 3 Ultra's RTL skill was built on a synthetic-data-generation pipeline that goes beyond spec-to-RTL generation to also create code-editing and debugging training tasks, injecting realistic bugs (incorrect FSM transitions, handshake/timing violations) into seed RTL and filtering all samples via syntax checks, benchmark decontamination, and an LLM-as-judge rubric scorer.
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: Task diversity in training data (not just data volume) appears to explain the model's edge on iterative debugging versus single-shot code generation — a reusable playbook other domain-specialized coding-LLM builders could copy for their own agentic niches.
insights.locator: The key innovation is task diversity

insights.claim: NVIDIA has secured integration commitments from all three major EDA vendors — Cadence, Siemens, and Synopsys — to embed Nemotron 3 Ultra into their agentic chip-design tools, positioning the open model as a shared backbone across the industry rather than a single-vendor point solution.
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: Broad EDA-incumbent buy-in de-risks NVIDIA's open-model distribution strategy and creates multiple monetization surfaces (Cadence ChipStack/InnoStack/ViraStack/AuraStack, Siemens Questa One/Fuse EDA, Synopsys AgentEngineer) — watch these vendors' product announcements for adoption signals.
insights.locator: Nemotron 3 Ultra is an open model and can be used today

insights.claim: Siemens claims its Fuse EDA AI Agent, paired with Nemotron 3 Ultra, powers long-running, self-verifying EDA agents at up to 5x-10x higher token efficiency.
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: An unverified vendor efficiency claim worth tracking for follow-up disclosure, as it would materially cut compute cost for long-running verification agents if substantiated.
insights.quote: integrated with Fuse EDA AI Agent for powering long-running, self-verifying EDA AI agents at up to 5x to 10x higher token efficiency
insights.locator: Siemens: Where Nemotron 3 Ultra pairs with the Questa One Agentic Toolkit

insights.claim: Synopsys says its AgentEngineer technology, built on Nemotron 3 Ultra with a continuous, traceable multi-agent feedback loop, can reduce weeks of manual verification effort to hours via its Openshell Sandbox.
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: A weeks-to-hours productivity claim is the kind of concrete ROI figure investors can probe Synopsys/customers on to gauge whether agentic verification tools are delivering real time savings versus marketing framing.
insights.quote: Its Openshell Sandbox can reduce weeks of manual verification effort to hours.

insights.claim: RTL correctness depends on precise temporal behavior and many bugs only surface during tool-based simulation, so real engineers iterate with compilers, simulators, lint tools, and waveform inspection rather than solving tasks in a single pass — making agentic, feedback-driven workflows structurally necessary rather than optional for chip design coding.
insights.speaker: Nirmal Kumar Juluru
insights.so_what: This structural need makes RTL a defensible niche for specialized agentic-AI vendors that is harder for generic single-shot coding copilots to commoditize, and explains why long-context efficiency (Nemotron's architecture) matters more here than in typical software-coding benchmarks.
insights.locator: Why RTL coding demands agentic workflows
